subject.title: [Feature]: Standardize skill data directory convention (configPaths) under ~/.openclaw/

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class per-skill runtime data directory contract, and if so should it be a filesystem convention, a plugin/skill API, or ClawHub authoring guidance?
rationale: The requested behavior creates a durable storage and metadata contract for third-party skills, and repository policy treats new storage/config/API surfaces as product and compatibility decisions rather than automatic cleanup.

options.title: Choose an API-backed data contract
options.body: Define one supported per-skill data contract in metadata/runtime/docs with install or doctor behavior only after the storage owner is clear.

options.title: Keep it as ClawHub guidance
options.body: Leave OpenClaw core unchanged and require skill publishers to document their own data paths through ClawHub packaging guidance.

options.title: Defer until a concrete skill breaks
options.body: Keep this in backlog but wait for higher-impact affected-skill evidence or missing API proof before designing a new surface.

recommendation.title: Choose an API-backed data contract
recommendation.body: Define one supported per-skill data contract in metadata/runtime/docs with install or doctor behavior only after the storage owner is clear.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent skills documentation/runtime history and product-boundary comments make this the best available routing candidate from the inspected history.
